s: Serverless key-value at absurd scale: consistent single-digit-ms latency regardless of table size.
w: Tables partition on hash key (+optional sort key for ranges). Throughput is provisioned (RCU/WCU) or on-demand; DynamoDB auto-splits hot partitions and replicates across AZs synchronously. DAX adds microsecond caching; Streams capture item changes for CDC; Global Tables approximate multi-region active-active with last-writer-wins.
use: Massive key-value/session/catalog lookups with known access patterns
Serverless architectures pairing functions with zero-ops storage
Games/IoT metadata where scale unpredictability kills provisioning guesses
avoid: Ad-hoc queries/joins - access patterns must be designed upfront (single-table design)
Complex transactions across many items (limited txn support exists but costly)

pat.d: One table, multiple GSIs, overloaded keys serve every access pattern.

pits: Hot partition on popular hash key - add suffixes/sharding buckets
Cost blowups scanning - always query by keys, use GSIs deliberately
tips: Frame as 'access-pattern-first' database; contrast with relational schema-first thinking
